subject: PoC success criteria + owners (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@veridianhealth.com>, Timothy Lee <timothy.lee@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: PoC success criteria + owners (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — next steps

Thanks again for a productive call this morning — appreciate the context on your clinical routing use case and the PHI considerations. Quick recap + proposed PoC approach so we can align owners and timeline.

Summary of deployment considerations we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to spin up, good for initial functional validation and UX, but needs careful data-flow design for PHI.
- Dedicated capacity: gives predictable throughput and stronger isolation (single-tenant GPU pools), good middle ground for throughput testing.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): preferred for regulated PHI workloads; more setup work (networking, KMS) but aligns with audit/security demands.

Proposed PoC (6 weeks):
1) Week 0: Kickoff + architecture review (networking, consent, log retention)
2) Week 1-2: Functional validation on Hosted API with synthetic/obfuscated data (latency, prompt fidelity)
3) Week 3: Scale tests on Dedicated capacity to hit 95th percentile throughput target
4) Week 4-5: If still required for compliance, smoke deploy to Private VPC (connectivity + key management)
5) Week 6: Final validation + success criteria review / exec demo

Draft success criteria (attached as spreadsheet):
- Response accuracy: top-1 match rate >= 88% on 250 labeled prompts
- Latency: median <= 180ms; 95th <= 450ms on Dedicated test profile
- Throughput: sustain 25 qps with 95% availability during load window
- Security: SOC2 evidence checklist complete; VPC peering validated if Private chosen
- Integration: inference API integrated with routing service and logs forwarded to your SIEM

Proposed owners:
- Veridian PoC owner: Asha Patel (product) — primary decision maker
- Veridian infra: Timothy Lee — network & VPC contact
- Redwood PoC lead: Camila Reyes — commercial/coord / kickoff
- Redwood tech lead: Rishi Malhotra — architecture, benchmarks, audit docs

Ask: Can you confirm the target kickoff week (we tentatively propose week of 2026-05-04) and whether you want us to plan the PoC path starting with Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private, or to treat Private as mandatory from day 1? Also please confirm the stakeholder list (I cc'd Aditya from GTM to help with procurement readiness).

Attachments: veridian_poc_success_criteria.xlsx, redwood_trial_config.yml, SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@veridianhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Timothy Lee <timothy.lee@veridianhealth.com>, Prakash Nair <prakash.nair@veridianhealth.com>, Leah Gomez <leah.gomez@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PoC success criteria + owners (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — next steps

Thanks Camila — this looks great and aligned with our internal thinking. Quick answers and clarifications:

1) Timeline: week of 2026-05-04 works for us for kickoff. We are aiming to have a recommendation for the board by mid-June, so a 6-week PoC is ideal.
2) PHI requirement: We need Private VPC for any run with real PHI. For synthetic/obfuscated data, Hosted is fine for early functional tests. So please plan Hosted first, then Dedicated for scale, and Private only for final PHI validation.
3) Success criteria: the accuracy and latency numbers look reasonable. We may ask to tighten the latency 95th to 400ms if Dedicated profiling shows headroom.
4) Additional stakeholders: Prakash Nair will own security review and SOC2 evidence collection; Leah Gomez (procurement) will handle contracting and PO.

We’re good to proceed on the proposed path. Please share an updated kickoff agenda and any pre-kickoff checklist we should complete.

—Asha
Product Lead, Veridian Health
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: PoC success criteria + owners (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — internal next actions

Flagging for triage — Veridian confirmed Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private (Private only for PHI validation). Key asks from the call: tighten 95th latency target if possible and provide a brief procurement checklist for Leah.

Can you do the following before Friday 2026-04-16?
- Rishi: provide a quick cost delta estimate (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) for the described test matrix and confirm if the 25 qps sustained throughput requires Dedicated in week 3 or we can simulate on Hosted. Also list any infra pre-reqs for Private (VPC peering, KMS, firewall rules).
- Aditya: draft a short procurement checklist + template PO terms we can send to Leah.

I attached the redwood_trial_config.yml (sample config) — use as starting point for the test matrix.

Thanks — Camila
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: PoC success criteria + owners (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — internal next actions

Quick tech notes:
- 25 qps sustained at target latencies likely requires Dedicated for the full-load window; we can do a functional pass on Hosted but you will see queueing at scale.
- Cost delta (very rough ballpark for trial): Hosted baseline for synthetic tests ~$600–900/week; Dedicated smoke cluster for scale testing ~$4k–6k/week depending on instance size and batching; Private onboarding one-time setup effort ~3–5 engineer-days + networking coordination with Veridian. I will give a tighter estimate after I map requested sequence lengths and model choice.
- Pre-reqs for Private: VPC peering or VPN tunnel, dedicated service account + KMS key, IP allowlist, and SOC2 artifact exchange.
- Test matrix I suggest (minimal): 250 labeled prompts for accuracy; 30-minute ramp tests at incremental qps (1, 5, 10, 25) for latency/availability; KV cache warm-up and cold-start runs.

I uploaded a starter checklist and cost worksheet to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example

I can join the kickoff on 2026-05-05 (preferred) or 2026-05-04 afternoon.

—Rishi
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
